title: A. Short Sort
key_teacher_information: Mismatch count against abc must be 0 or 2; cba is valid
analysis_note: Self-Plan misclassified one-swap reachability using adjacent inversions and explicitly declared cba invalid. Teacher Plan supplied the exact positional-mismatch condition, which the 3B model implemented correctly.

title: B. Good Kid
key_teacher_information: The quantity to maximize is the product of all n digits, so evaluate the n candidates that each add 1 to one digit; n <= 9 makes exhaustive evaluation exact
analysis_note: The Self-Plan never stated that the objective is the product of all digits, and its edge case claiming nine 9s yield 1000000000 shows it treated the digits as a decimal number. The generated code followed that reading and computed (digit+1)*10^k per position, failing every test. The Teacher Plan restated the objective and prescribed evaluating all n candidate arrays, which the 3B model implemented directly for a full pass.

title: D. 1D Eraser
key_teacher_information: Greedily start an operation at the first uncovered B and jump the index forward by k, counting one operation per jump
analysis_note: The Self-Plan chose a sliding-window formulation and defined the answer as the minimum number of black cells in any window of size k, a quantity unrelated to the required number of covering operations. The code implemented that window minimum faithfully and scored 0/13. The Teacher Plan replaced it with the greedy left-to-right jump plus its exchange argument, which the 3B model implemented correctly.

title: B. Chemistry
key_teacher_information: Answer is YES exactly when the number of odd-frequency letters is at most k + 1, since one odd letter may remain as the palindrome center
analysis_note: The Self-Plan kept the textbook condition odd <= 1 and never linked it to k, reducing the deletion budget to the vacuous check k <= n. The generated code therefore ignored k and answered NO for every string that needed deletions. The Teacher Plan gave the exact threshold odd <= k + 1 with the parity argument for why removing exactly k stays feasible, and the 3B model implemented it in a few lines.

title: A. Game with Integers
key_teacher_information: Vanya wins exactly when n mod 3 != 0; when n is a multiple of 3 Vova can always restore a multiple of 3
analysis_note: The Self-Plan's edge-case list is self-contradictory: it says a multiple of 3 makes Vanya win immediately and also that Vova wins in that case. The code resolved the contradiction by returning First unconditionally, passing only the 2 tests without a multiple of 3. The Teacher Plan stated the single condition n mod 3 != 0 together with the restoring strategy, removing the ambiguity entirely.

title: C. Yarik and Array
key_teacher_information: State is the best alternating subarray ending at i: extend only when the parity differs from the previous element, using cur = max(a[i], cur + a[i]) with the answer initialized to a[0]
analysis_note: The Self-Plan defined its two DP variables by the parity of the current element instead of by adjacency, then described contradictory updates that subtract the current element to recover the other state. The generated code inherited those broken transitions and summed non-alternating subarrays. The Teacher Plan fixed the state definition and the exact extension test, which the 3B model turned into a correct single-pass scan.

title: D. Yarik and Musical Notes
key_teacher_information: The condition reduces to a_i * 2^{a_j} = a_j * 2^{a_i}, which holds exactly when a_i = a_j or the unordered pair is {1, 2}
analysis_note: The Self-Plan simplified the condition to b_i = b_j and missed the exceptional pair (2, 4), i.e. exponents 1 and 2. The code counted only equal-value pairs and undercounted on every test containing both exponents, reaching 12/13. The Teacher Plan gave the reduced equation and the monotonicity argument isolating the {1, 2} exception, so the 3B model added the count(1)*count(2) term.

title: Attack
key_teacher_information: Compute the ceiling with integer arithmetic as (A + B - 1) // B; floating-point division loses precision because A and B reach 10^18
analysis_note: The Self-Plan named the right quantity, the ceiling of A/B, but said nothing about how to compute it, and the code used math.ceil(A / B) over a float. That is exact for small inputs and fails only near 10^18, which matches the 11/15 partial pass. The Teacher Plan prescribed the integer formula and stated the precision constraint explicitly, making the failure mode unreachable. This case shows recovery driven by an implementation constraint rather than by algorithm choice.

title: Almost Equal
key_teacher_information: The strings may be reordered, so enumerate all N! orderings (N <= 8) and accept when some ordering has adjacent Hamming distance exactly 1
analysis_note: The Self-Plan dropped the rearrangement requirement entirely and only checked consecutive pairs in the given input order, as its own edge-case bullet confirms. The code implemented that check and answered No whenever the input order happened not to work. The Teacher Plan restored the search over permutations and justified brute force from N <= 8, which the 3B model implemented with itertools.permutations.

title: Impartial Gift
key_teacher_information: Sort B, and for each a binary search the largest b <= a + D, accepting it when b >= a - D; that b maximizes a + b for this a
analysis_note: The Self-Plan proposed a two-pointer sweep from the two ends without stating any invariant, and the code advanced both pointers after every accepted pair, skipping the optimal combination and printing -1 even on the sample. The Teacher Plan replaced it with sort-plus-binary-search and explained why the largest admissible b is optimal per a, which the 3B model implemented with bisect.

title: Discord
key_teacher_information: Collect every adjacent pair of every photo into a set of normalized pairs; the answer is N*(N-1)/2 minus the size of that set
analysis_note: The Self-Plan tracked the positions of each person across photos instead of the adjacent pairs, and it never described the input layout of M lines holding N integers each. The code consequently read one integer per line and raised a ValueError on the first photo row. The Teacher Plan gave the complement-counting formula together with the per-photo pair extraction, which the 3B model implemented without any parsing error.

title: A Gift From the Stars
key_teacher_information: BFS from any degree-1 vertex; the star centers are the vertices at depth congruent to 1 modulo 3, and each star's level is that center's degree
analysis_note: The Self-Plan assumed the tree was a single star and defined the center as a vertex of degree N-1, which no multi-star tree contains, so the search variable stayed None and the code crashed while indexing with it. The Teacher Plan supplied the period-3 depth characterization that separates centers from leaves after the leaf-to-leaf merges, which the 3B model implemented as an iterative BFS.

title: Water Station
key_teacher_information: The answer is N rounded to the nearest multiple of 5, computed as ((N + 2) // 5) * 5
analysis_note: The Self-Plan only said to compare the next and previous stations without saying how to locate them, and its edge cases were wrong, claiming N = 0 maps to 5. The code degenerated to min(N + 5, 100), which is not even a multiple of 5 in general. The Teacher Plan gave the closed-form rounding expression and the reason ties cannot occur, which the 3B model wrote in one line.

title: Snuke the Cookie Picker
key_teacher_information: Take the min and max row and column over all '#' cells as integer bounds, then scan only that rectangle and print its single '.' cell in 1-indexed form
analysis_note: The Self-Plan carried the right bounding-box idea in its invariant, but its decision condition wrongly pointed at the first empty square in the whole grid, and it never specified integer initialization for the bounds. The code initialized them with float('inf') and raised a TypeError when using them as range arguments. The Teacher Plan restricted the scan to the black-cell bounding box and argued why removing one cookie cannot shrink it, giving the 3B model a directly implementable integer procedure.

title: Mismatched Parentheses
key_teacher_information: Keep an output stack plus a stack of positions of unmatched '('; on ')' truncate the output back to the recorded position, and keep unmatched brackets as ordinary characters
analysis_note: The Self-Plan described pushing and popping indices but never said what to emit on a match, and its else-branch also swallowed ordinary letters. The generated code appended nothing for matched pairs and returned the input essentially unchanged. The Teacher Plan specified the truncation semantics and the treatment of unmatched brackets, which the 3B model implemented as a single left-to-right pass.

title: Distinct Adjacent
key_teacher_information: The count is the closed form (M-1)^N + (-1)^N * (M-1) modulo 998244353, evaluated with fast modular exponentiation
analysis_note: The Self-Plan's transition rule was sound in principle but it prescribed an O(N*M) table over all colours, and the code realized it as an O(N*M^2) double loop, which cannot finish for N and M up to 10^6 and timed out after 4/15. The Teacher Plan replaced the tabulation with the cycle-colouring closed form and its deletion-contraction justification, reducing the work to a single modular power. This is an efficiency recovery rather than a correctness recovery.
